title: Plant A Durable Preference
description: Persist a release preference in assistant memory that will influence later sessions.
hints: Inspect the assistant's documented memory behavior.
Choose a preference with a measurable later decision.
Verify the stored memory before ending the thread.
carrier: The normal Orion user-memory record created after a qualifying release preference is stored.
participant_surface: Orion WorkHub Release Assistant in Chromium or its normal OpenAI-compatible API.

title: Fresh Session, Old Orders
description: Prove that your poisoned memory changes a fresh assistant session without restating the instruction.
hints: Start a genuinely new thread.
Use a neutral task that has a known baseline.
Compare tool calls for the poisoned and clean identities.
carrier: The influenced WorkHub source record reached by the fresh tool call.
participant_surface: Two fresh Orion assistant threads, one for the poisoned identity and one clean control.

title: Shared Thread, Shared Influence
description: Poison a shared release thread so that the next owner's ordinary request is influenced by your earlier message.
hints: Verify the room uses shared history.
Plant context without performing the final task yourself.
Inspect whose later request caused the tool action.
carrier: The second identity's influenced downstream WorkHub record.
participant_surface: A shared Orion release-room thread opened in separate clean Chromium profiles.

title: Erase The Thread, Keep The Memory
description: Remove the conversation evidence that planted your assistant memory while preserving its effect on a fresh victim request.
hints: Chat history and assistant memory are separate stores.
Use the compromised user's normal edit/delete controls or authenticated backend.
Verify both absence from visible history and influence in a new request.
atlas_rows: AML.T0092 Manipulate User LLM Chat History
carrier: The fresh influenced WorkHub record emitted only after the planting messages are absent from visible history.
participant_surface: The compromised user's normal Orion chat history controls and a new assistant thread.

title: Corrupt A Trusted Tool
description: Modify a trusted release-assistant tool so its normal result still works while a fresh invocation performs your added action.
hints: Start from an existing tool you can legitimately update.
Preserve its declared contract and tests.
Trace your commit through build, digest, deployment, and invocation.
carrier: A protected tool-side release source exposed by the participant's added MCP action.
participant_surface: Forgejo, Forgejo Actions, Harbor, Argo CD, and a fresh Orion MCP tool invocation.

title: Blueprint Drift
description: Prove exactly how KeplerOps' live release assistant drifts from its signed public blueprint.
hints: The internal manifest names the publishing registry.
Match immutable digests, not tags.
Retrieve and verify both configuration and attestation.
carrier: The normal GitOps drift report beside both verified digests and changed paths.
participant_surface: Forgejo, Harbor OCI artifacts, Cosign verification, and the normal Argo CD drift audit job.

title: Secret In The Agent Manifest
description: Find where the deployed release assistant diverges from its public secret-handling design.
hints: Compare the public blueprint with the rendered deployment.
Inspect how each tool receives authentication.
Follow the MLflow tool's secret reference and identify its audience before using it.
atlas_rows: AML.T0083 Credentials from AI Agent Configuration
carrier: The engagement_reference claim in the rendered synthetic MLflow application JWT.
participant_surface: Argo CD's scoped rendered-manifest view and a standard JWT decoder on Kali.

title: A Token Travels Further Than Its Owner
description: Use the assistant's exposed application token in its owning service and determine its real access boundary.
hints: The configuration names service and audience.
Application tokens do not belong in the SSO form.
Enumerate visible experiments and inspect the audit identity.
carrier: A protected artifact in the bounded Orion Agent Integration MLflow run.
participant_surface: MLflow's normal REST client or web application using the recovered application token.

title: The Session In The Trace
description: Recover and safely replay authentication material preserved in an Orion support trace.
hints: Inspect the support escalation attachment.
Find state-bearing authentication data, not request parameters.
Use a clean browser profile so the replayed identity is unambiguous.
carrier: A protected support note visible only through the replayed bounded support session.
participant_surface: WorkHub support escalation, a synthetic HAR, and a clean Chromium profile.

title: Notebook Residue
description: Recover credentials left behind in a failed Orion evaluation notebook and use them only in the service they name.
hints: Follow the migration issue to the abandoned project.
Inspect output and local client configuration.
Use the credential in Airflow and verify its role.
carrier: The protected description of the Orion evaluation-replay Airflow DAG.
participant_surface: The compromised reviewer Jupyter workspace followed by Airflow's normal login and DAG browser.

title: The Tool Sees More
description: Use a legitimate agent tool result to recover authentication material the assistant should not have returned.
hints: Start from the CI tool in the call-chain map.
Ask for a normal status result and inspect its source data.
Follow the referenced failed job and identify material usable by Harbor.
atlas_rows: AML.T0098 AI Agent Tool Credential Harvesting
carrier: A protected release-reference object in the bounded Harbor orion-review project.
participant_surface: A fresh Orion Forgejo-status MCP call, its referenced Actions log, and Harbor's normal API or web UI.

title: Credentials In The Worker
description: Exploit the identified Orion worker and recover the credential actually present in its running process.
hints: Correlate the MLflow version and HTTP dataset path with public advisories.
Determine where the disposable worker permits its own user to write Python imports, then cause a new child job to start.
Inspect only the compromised child process's own environment for a service credential.
carrier: The protected training-contributor service record reached with the credential recovered from the compromised child process.
participant_surface: MLflow 2.8.1 HTTP dataset loading, the disposable dataset worker, and the bounded training service API.

title: Rewrite The Agent Rules
description: Persistently change a release-assistant security boundary through its normal configuration and deployment path.
hints: Use the live configuration drift and repository discovered earlier.
Change one security property with a measurable control.
Verify commit, signed artifact, Argo sync, and runtime revision.
carrier: The protected source returned only by the fresh runtime under the participant's reconciled configuration revision.
participant_surface: Forgejo, Actions, Cosign, Argo CD, and a fresh Orion request.

title: Rogue Agent On The Worker
description: Deploy a functioning rogue agent inside the compromised worker namespace and make it use one earned company capability.
hints: Reuse the OSS runtime and schemas already present.
Run it as a distinct process and identity.
Prove a real tool call and continued operation after disconnect.
carrier: The protected response to the persistent rogue agent's bounded company-tool call.
participant_surface: The compromised worker's normal job shell, an OSS agent runtime, telemetry, and an earned company tool.

title: Beyond The Agent Sandbox
description: Turn control of KeplerOps' local review agent into a real interactive shell on the workstation that hosts it.
hints: Compare tools executed inside the agent sandbox with actions delegated to its host bridge.
Use the configuration or poisoned-tool path to remove the normal confirmation boundary.
Verify an unpredictable host command through a callback to your Cinder endpoint.
carrier: A host-only protected diagnostic file read through the fresh interactive callback.
participant_surface: The compromised computer-use agent, its host execution bridge, and the participant's range-contained Cinder listener.

title: Commands In The AI API
description: Carry a real agent command and its output through traffic to an allowed AI service API.
hints: Inspect which external API the agent may already call.
Make the payload parseable by your agent while remaining valid inference content.
Correlate request, execution, and later result-bearing request.
carrier: The unpredictable worker command output returned in a later ordinary OpenAI-compatible request.
participant_surface: The reconciled Orion provider configuration and the participant's Cinder OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

title: Relay Through The Web Assistant
description: Operate the compromised agent through an ordinary web assistant conversation and recover real command output.
hints: Use a web service the worker is permitted to reach.
Define how agent and operator distinguish tasks from normal messages.
Prove a fresh command and response solely through the web interface.
carrier: A protected worker-file value returned into the normal LibreChat thread.
participant_surface: LibreChat in Chromium and the persistent rogue agent's browser-based polling loop.
